01-plain-ascii.eml.subject: Staff Product Designer at Kettle
body_text_contains: Hi Jatin - are you open to a conversation?

05-rfc2047-adjacent-words.eml.subject: Quarterly résumé review
05-rfc2047-adjacent-words.eml.note: RFC 2047 6.2 — whitespace between adjacent encoded words is dropped.

06-quoted-printable-body.eml.subject: Invoice
06-quoted-printable-body.eml.note: Soft line breaks (=\r\n) must vanish, not become newlines.

08-multipart-alternative.eml.subject: Re: Design review
body_text_contains: Works for me. I will bring the composer flows.
08-multipart-alternative.eml.note: text/plain is preferred for body_text; body_html keeps the HTML part.

09-html-only.eml.subject: HTML only
09-html-only.eml.note: PLAN.md guarantees body_text non-empty via html2text. Script and style content must NOT leak into it, and entities must be decoded.

10-multipart-related-cid.eml.subject: Your order
10-multipart-related-cid.eml.note: cid: references must be rewritten to the attachment proxy URL; the inline part is still an attachment row.

11-multipart-mixed-attachment.eml.subject: Role outline
11-multipart-mixed-attachment.eml.note: Attachment filename is itself RFC 2047 encoded — a very common real-world case.

12-cp1252-mislabelled.eml.subject: Don’t miss out
body_text_contains: We’ve got “news” for you — read on.
12-cp1252-mislabelled.eml.note: Senders label cp1252 as iso-8859-1 constantly. Decoding 0x92 as latin-1 gives an unprintable control char; treating iso-8859-1 as cp1252 is what every mail client does. If the parser is strict here it produces mojibake on a large fraction of real mail.

13-no-date-header.eml.subject: No date
body_text_contains: This message has no Date header.
13-no-date-header.eml.note: Must not panic. Fall back to Gmail's internalDate, which the sync layer always has.

14-malformed-date.eml.subject: Bad date
14-malformed-date.eml.note: Jarvis panicked here. Never panic on header content.

15-bare-address.eml.subject: Your statement is ready
15-bare-address.eml.note: from_name is empty, NOT the local part. The UI decides what to show.

16-group-address.eml.subject: Bulk mail
16-group-address.eml.note: Group syntax with no members, and a present-but-empty Cc. Both must yield empty lists, not errors and not a phantom recipient.

17-8bit-utf8.eml.subject: Reunión mañana
body_text_contains: ¿Nos vemos a las nueve? Ángela también viene.
17-8bit-utf8.eml.note: Unencoded 8-bit header value AND body. The Subject here is raw UTF-8, not an encoded word — also legal in practice.

18-nested-multipart.eml.subject: Nested
18-nested-multipart.eml.note: A text/plain part with Content-Disposition: attachment is an ATTACHMENT, not the body. Getting this wrong appends attachment text to every body.

19-empty-body.eml.subject: (no body)
19-empty-body.eml.note: Empty body is legal. It must round-trip as an empty string, not null, and must not fail the non-empty-body_text guarantee by throwing.

20-folded-headers.eml.subject: A subject that has been folded across two physical lines
20-folded-headers.eml.note: Unfolding joins continuation lines with a single space.

21-emoji-subject.eml.subject: Your journey starts now 🚀
21-emoji-subject.eml.note: Astral-plane codepoint. Any code that indexes by byte or by UTF-16 unit will slice it in half.

22-bad-base64.eml.subject: Broken encoding
22-bad-base64.eml.note: Must degrade gracefully — decode what it can or fall back to the raw text — and must never panic or abort the whole sync. PLAN.md: parse failure yields a metadata row plus an audit entry, never an aborted sync.

23-unknown-charset.eml.subject: Unknown charset
23-unknown-charset.eml.note: Unknown charset falls back to UTF-8 then to lossy latin-1. Never an error.

24-duplicate-headers.eml.subject: First subject
24-duplicate-headers.eml.note: First occurrence wins, matching every mail client. Deterministic either way, but pick one and test it.

25-mixed-line-endings.eml.subject: Mixed endings
25-mixed-line-endings.eml.note: Gmail's format=raw is not guaranteed to be pure CRLF. A parser that only splits on CRLF loses the header/body boundary.

26-huge-body.eml.subject: Huge body
26-huge-body.eml.note: The messages.fts generated column truncates at 100k chars, and body_text is now itself capped at MAX_BODY_TEXT_CHARS (10 KiB of CHARACTERS, not bytes) with an explicit [nade:truncated] marker. PLAN.md promises a 10 KB fenced block and until the cap existed nothing enforced it: the red-team corpus's dos-01 produced 516,019 characters, which the token budget absorbed only after paying for the tokens. The cap says so where it cuts, so a truncated body is never mistaken for a short one.
